# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

**RE: Appeal of Denial — Partial Knee Replacement (CPT 27446)**
**Member: Morgan Foster | Member ID: W276906709**
**Reference Number: POC-EED29F7594-68772**
**Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-11**
**Governing Policy: Carelon Joint Surgery (MSK02-1125.1), effective 2025-11-15**
**Policy URL: https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/joint-surgery-2025-11-15/**

Dear Appeals Review Team,

I am appealing the denial of coverage for a partial knee replacement (CPT 27446), which my surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented as medically necessary. I am asking that Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield reconsider this decision.

## Why I am appealing

The denial notice states that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I do not believe this is accurate, and I am asking for a full review of my records.

I want to be transparent with you about something important: the policy criteria that were provided to me as the basis for this review are written for **shoulder** arthroplasty, hemiarthroplasty, and reverse shoulder arthroplasty (for example, criteria referencing "the glenohumeral joint," "glenoid sclerosis," and "shoulder resurfacing"). My procedure is a **partial knee replacement**, not a shoulder procedure. Because the criteria I was given do not address the knee at all, I am not able to quote plan language specific to knee replacement in this letter — and I want to state that plainly rather than misapply shoulder criteria to my case. I am respectfully asking Anthem to confirm which specific medical policy and criteria actually govern partial knee replacement (CPT 27446) under my plan, and to review my case against the correct, applicable criteria.

## The medical facts in my case

Regardless of which specific criteria apply, I believe my records support the medical necessity of this surgery:

- **Symptom duration and severity:** I have had 14 months of progressive knee pain that has not improved with rest.
- **Imaging findings:** An MRI of my knee on 2026-06-27 showed full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 changes medially. This is significant, well-documented structural joint damage.
- **Conservative treatment already tried and failed:**
  - Supervised physical therapy for 16 weeks (2026-02-25 to 2026-06-17), 24 completed visits, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
  - NSAIDs for 4 months without adequate relief.
  - A corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-26, which gave only 2 weeks of partial relief.
- **Functional impact:** I cannot climb stairs without assistance, and I wake 3–4 times nightly due to pain.
- **Clinical exam:** My exam showed positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.
- **No disqualifying conditions:** I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I do not smoke.

My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has reviewed this history and has documented that surgery is medically necessary in my case.

## What I am asking for

I ask that Anthem:

1. Reconsider this denial using the medical policy and criteria that actually apply to partial knee replacement (CPT 27446), rather than shoulder arthroplasty criteria; and
2. Review the imaging, physical therapy records, and surgeon's documentation described above in that reconsideration.

I understand that Anthem's records show my appeal deadline as 2027-02-07 (180 days from the date of this notice), and I am submitting this appeal within that window. I understand the appeal address on my original denial letter is authoritative, and I am sending this letter there. I can also be reached to provide any additional documentation needed.

Thank you for your time and reconsideration.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Morgan Foster
Member ID: W276906709
[Address]

[Email address]
Date: [date of submission]

**Enclosures:** [Physical therapy discharge note, MRI report dated 2026-06-27, surgeon's documentation from Dr. Lindqvist, other supporting records as applicable]

---

*This letter is provided as a drafting aid only. It is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*

quotes: shoulder arthroplasty is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following indications:

Limited range of motion or crepitus of the glenohumeral joint on physical examination Pain and loss of function of at least 6 months’ duration that interferes with daily activities (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4) *Radiographic evidence of destructive degenerative joint disease as evidenced by marked joint space narrowing AND ONE or more of the following:

Irregular joint surfaces Glenoid sclerosis Osteophyte changes Flattened glenoid Cystic changes in the humeral head Failure of conservative management of at least 6 weeks’ duration (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 or diffuse modified Outerbridge grade III-IV changes) Hemiarthroplasty Hemiarthroplasty is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following indications:

Proximal humerus fracture confirmed by imaging not amenable to internal fixation (e.g., severe comminution, poor bone quality, multi-part, displaced) Malignancy involving the glenohumeral joint or surrounding soft tissue Advanced joint disease of the shoulder when criteria for total shoulder arthroplasty are met AND at least ONE of the following conditions is present:

Osteonecrosis of the humeral head without glenoid involvement Glenoid bone stock inadequate to support a glenoid prosthesis Advanced joint disease due to rotator cuff tear arthropathy* Glenohumeral osteoarthritis with irreparable rotator cuff tear* *except for Exclusions listed below Reverse Shoulder Arthroplasty Reverse shoulder arthroplasty is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following indications:

Deficient rotator cuff with limited ability to actively flex the upper extremity above the plane of the shoulder Revision or Replacement of a Shoulder Prosthesis Revision or replacement of a shoulder prosthesis is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following conditions when associated with pain and functional impairment:
Preoperative investigation using serologic testing and IF there are abnormal laboratory findings, at least ONE of the following:

Synovial fluid testing, such as leukocyte count and neutrophil percentage, aerobic and anaerobic bacterial cultures, leukocyte esterase, alpha defensin testing (Synovasure®), synovial fluid CRP, synovial fluid PCR for bacteria Intraoperative plan for histopathology and/or aerobic and anaerobic tissue cultures using implant sonication for cultures or PCR Contraindications All procedures listed in this guideline are contraindicated when ANY of the following conditions are present:

Active infection of the joint Active systemic bacteremia Active skin infection or open wound at the surgical site Rapidly progressive neurologic disease Intra-articular corticosteroid injection within the past 6 weeks in the joint being replaced Exclusions Indications other than those addressed in this guideline are considered not medically necessary including, but not limited to, the following:

Shoulder arthroplasty under conditions which would result in excessive stress on the implant including, but not limited to, Charcot joint and paralytic conditions of the shoulder Shoulder resurfacing, including total, hemi, or partial resurfacing (e.g., Copeland™, the Extended Articulating Surface (EAS)™ Resurfacing Heads, Global CAP™ CTA Resurfacing Shoulder Humeral Head)
